blocks.content: I packed up around 9:15. Closed the sketchbook, capped the pencils, zipped the bag. The drawing was still in there. I wasn't going to take it out. I was just going to close the book and move on with the day.
Mr. Alvarez materialized at my elbow with his rag.
Going out to paint from life.
Travel easel. Some oils. The sketchbook.
He nodded slowly, like he was deciding something.
Your clouds still look like mashed potatoes.
You told me that six months ago.
I laughed. I always do. He knows that.
I stood and shouldered my bag. The morning outside was fully itself now — people on the street, the light gone flat and even, the quiet version of the town already replaced.
Sometimes a painting finds you before you find it.
I looked at him for a moment.
I don't know what that means.
